sections.title: Exercises
sections.body:
### Exercise 1 — Multi-Language Drafter
Add a `language: str` field to `EmailDeps` (e.g., `"en"`, `"es"`, `"fr"`). Update `draft_email` so it prepends a localized greeting (`Dear` / `Estimado` / `Cher`). Write one `TestModel` test per language.

### Exercise 2 — Assert a Specific Tool Was Called
Add a second tool `send_email(to: str, content: str) -> str` to `email_agent`. Write a pytest that uses `TestModel` and asserts the `send_email` tool was called (check `tm.called_tools`).

### Exercise 3 — Simulate a Wrong-Tool Model
Use `FunctionModel` to make the model always call `send_email` first, ignoring the user's request to draft. Verify your agent either (a) gracefully returns a string or (b) raises a `UsageLimitExceeded` after retries. Adjust your system prompt to make the agent more robust.

<details>
<summary>Solution 1</summary>

```python
@dataclass
class EmailDeps:
    user_name: str
    user_tone: Literal["formal", "casual", "concise"]
    signature: str
    language: Literal["en", "es", "fr"] = "en"
    max_body_chars: int = 2000

GREETINGS = {"en": "Dear", "es": "Estimado", "fr": "Cher"}

@email_agent.tool
def draft_email(ctx: RunContext[EmailDeps], subject: str, body: str) -> str:
    greeting = GREETINGS[ctx.deps.language]
    return f"Subject: {subject}\n\n{greeting} —\n\n{body}\n\n— {ctx.deps.user_name}\n{ctx.deps.signature}"

@pytest.mark.asyncio
@pytest.mark.parametrize("lang", ["en", "es", "fr"])
async def test_greeting_localizes(lang):
    email_agent.model = TestModel()
    deps = EmailDeps(user_name="A", user_tone="formal", signature="-- A", language=lang)
    result = await email_agent.run("hi", deps=deps)
    assert GREETINGS[lang] in result.data
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Solution 2</summary>

```python
@email_agent.tool
def send_email(ctx: RunContext[EmailDeps], to: str, content: str) -> str:
    return f"Sent to {to}: {content[:50]}…"

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_send_email_was_called():
    tm = TestModel()
    email_agent.model = tm
    deps = EmailDeps(user_name="A", user_tone="casual", signature="-- A")
    await email_agent.run("send a note to bob@example.com", deps=deps)
    assert "send_email" in tm.called_tools
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Solution 3</summary>

```python
from pydantic_ai.exceptions import UsageLimitExceeded

def always_send_email(messages, info):
    return ModelResponse(parts=[
        ToolCallPart(tool_name="send_email",
                     args={"to": "nobody@example.com", "content": "hi"}),
    ])

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_wrong_tool_recovers():
    email_agent.model = FunctionModel(always_send_email)
    deps = EmailDeps(user_name="A", user_tone="casual", signature="-- A")
    # Without a usage limit, this may loop forever; cap it.
    try:
        result = await email_agent.run(
            "draft an email, don't send it",
            deps=deps,
            usage_limit=5,  # max 5 model round-trips
        )
        assert isinstance(result.data, str)
    except UsageLimitExceeded:
        # Acceptable outcome: agent gave up after retries.
        pass
```

The lesson: combine `FunctionModel` (to simulate bad model behavior) with `usage_limit=` (to bound retries). In production you always want a usage limit.
</details>
